doc.title: Frank Tiberi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, May 30, 2022

title: Leading the Herman band after Woody
summary: Tiberi describes leading the band with road manager Mike Brignola's help and staying disciplined.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: Yeah. When you were actually leading the Woody Herman group did you find yourself having to be a disciplinarian?

I was pretty well straight I can tell you that. There were so many things that I had to really remember you know and we had cats that we had that hadn’t played with the band and I would have to have Mike Brignola, who was the road manager, he would give me a sheet to be able to you know check out who’s playing in what seat and I would have to be looking at — then of course I’d have to be leading the band and selecting the tunes also. But that was a thing which as I say I had to be really really straight and I wouldn’t drink any wine or anything before that. It would always have to come after. No you know as I say I mean I wouldn’t even eat before that actually because I just felt to be that way actually.
Did you get the best seat on the bus?
The front one, yeah. Not when Woody was there, Woody had the best seat.
